characters.role: the reader / main character, the band leader
a chirpy parrot who sings along

coverMeta.dedication: For everyone who ever hummed a little too loud.

pages.text: The backyard was warm and buzzing, because tonight your band was playing its very first neighborhood show. You set up two folding chairs, a bucket of drumsticks, and a wobbly music stand. {{FRIEND_NAME}} marched in, tapping a drumstick on everything. "Okay, team, listen up! We start with a giant drumroll, and it is going to be amazing," {{FRIEND_NAME}} announced. Behind the flowerpots, {{SECOND_NAME}} peeked out and whispered, "Maybe... a quiet song first? Just to warm up?" On your shoulder, {{PET_NAME}} bobbed up and down and squawked, "Warm up! Tweet! Warm up!" You grinned, because you were the band leader, and the first choice was yours.

choices.text: Start big with {{FRIEND_NAME}}'s drumroll.
Start soft with {{SECOND_NAME}}'s quiet song.

pages.text: "Yes! Now you are thinking like a drummer!" {{FRIEND_NAME}} cheered, spinning a drumstick in the air and almost dropping it. {{FRIEND_NAME}} counted loud and proud, "One, two, three, and a boom, boom, BOOM!" The buckets rumbled like happy thunder, and the fence rattled a friendly little rattle. {{SECOND_NAME}} covered both ears and giggled, "That is very... loud. But kind of wonderful." {{PET_NAME}} flapped in a circle and shouted, "Boom, boom! Pretty bird! Boom!" You laughed so hard you had to sit down on the wobbly chair.

choices.text: Teach {{PET_NAME}} to end the drumroll with a squawk.
Invite shy {{SECOND_NAME}} up to sing over the drums.

pages.text: "A quiet song. I can do a quiet song," {{SECOND_NAME}} said softly, holding the microphone with both hands. You hummed a gentle starting note, and {{SECOND_NAME}} began to sing, small at first, like a tiptoe. "Fine, fine, we can be gentle for exactly one song," {{FRIEND_NAME}} said, tapping the buckets so lightly it sounded like rain. {{PET_NAME}} tilted its head, listened, and then cooed along, "Coo... coo... la la la." It was so pretty that a neighbor leaned over the fence just to hear.

choices.text: Cheer {{SECOND_NAME}} on to sing a little louder.
Let {{FRIEND_NAME}} sneak in a soft drum beat.

pages.text: You clapped your hands and called out, "{{CHILD_NAME}} says: everyone in for the big finish rehearsal!" {{FRIEND_NAME}} pointed a drumstick like a wizard's wand and declared, "Rule number one, I count us in. Rule number two, nobody argues with rule number one." {{SECOND_NAME}} raised a shy hand and whispered, "Could rule number three be... we all smile?" "Approved!" boomed {{FRIEND_NAME}}, grinning. {{PET_NAME}} landed on the music stand and announced, "Smile! Tweet! Best band! Smile!" and everyone cracked up.

choices.text: Practice the ending where the drums go quiet.
Practice the ending where everybody sings together.

pages.text: "Come on up, you can do it," you said, and gently waved {{SECOND_NAME}} toward the microphone. {{SECOND_NAME}} took one big breath and squeaked, "Okay. But if I turn pink, we all pretend it is the sunset." "Deal! Now sing over my mega beat!" {{FRIEND_NAME}} said, drumming a bouncy rhythm. {{SECOND_NAME}}'s voice wobbled, then grew, then floated right over the drums like a kite. {{PET_NAME}} bounced on your shoulder and cheered, "Sing it! Sing it! Whee!"

choices.text: Practice the big group ending.
Let {{PET_NAME}} try a solo squawk.

pages.text: {{FRIEND_NAME}} tiptoed to the buckets and whispered, which was very hard for {{FRIEND_NAME}}, "I am being so quiet right now. This is the quietest I have ever been." A soft beat pattered under {{SECOND_NAME}}'s singing, and the two sounds fit together like a puzzle. "Oh," {{SECOND_NAME}} breathed, "it sounds nice when we take turns." You nodded, because taking turns was the secret all along. {{PET_NAME}} whispered too, a tiny "coo... coo," and even the crickets seemed to hush and listen.

choices.text: Add a gentle drum ending.
Add a soft owl-like coo ending.

pages.text: "Here comes the tricky part, so eyes on me," {{FRIEND_NAME}} said, lifting both drumsticks high. "When I go like this, everybody stops at exactly the same time. Snap. Like magic." {{SECOND_NAME}} bit a lip and murmured, "What if I sing one extra note by accident?" You smiled and said, "Then it will be the best accident ever." {{PET_NAME}} bobbed and promised, "Stop! Tweet! I stop good!" You practiced the snap-stop three times, and by the third time it really did feel like magic.

choices.text: Finish getting ready for the show.
Take a wobbly-chair bow to celebrate the great rehearsal.

pages.text: "Everybody together on the last line, that is the whole trick," you said, standing tall. {{FRIEND_NAME}} grinned. "Together? Fine, but I am still the loudest together-er." {{SECOND_NAME}} laughed, actually laughed out loud this time, and said, "Then I will be the sweetest together-er." {{PET_NAME}} flapped and declared, "I am the tweetest together-er! Tweet!" You all sang the last line at once, and it sounded warm and round and just right.

choices.text: Do one last full run-through.
Decide you are ready right now.

pages.text: You decided the ending should drift away soft, like a leaf landing. {{SECOND_NAME}} sang the last note so gently it was almost a secret. "That is beautiful," {{FRIEND_NAME}} admitted, resting the drumsticks. "Do not tell anyone I said beautiful." "Too late," you teased, and everyone giggled. {{PET_NAME}} closed the whole thing with a slow, proud "cooooo," then added, "Encore! Tweet! Encore!" You realized the band was truly ready.

choices.text: Head to the front yard for showtime.
Celebrate the perfect soft ending.

pages.text: The neighbors were gathering now, setting out lawn chairs and sipping lemonade. {{FRIEND_NAME}} peeked around the gate and gasped, "Whoa. That is a lot of ears out there." {{SECOND_NAME}} squeezed your hand and whispered, "My tummy has butterflies. Big ones. With drums." You squeezed back and said, "Butterflies mean you care. We have got this, together." {{PET_NAME}} puffed up its feathers and announced to everyone, "Show time! Best band! Tweet tweet!"

choices.text: Start the show with the loud, joyful version.
Start the show with the sweet, gentle version.

pages.text: You did not even wait for showtime, because right now felt too good to save. You all took a big silly bow off the wobbly chair, and the chair squeaked like it was clapping. "That," said {{FRIEND_NAME}}, wiping a happy tear, "was our best rehearsal in the history of best rehearsals." {{SECOND_NAME}} beamed and whispered, "I was not even a little pink. Well, maybe a little." {{PET_NAME}} landed on your head and crowned the moment with a proud "Tweet! We did it!" The show could wait five more minutes, because a band this happy deserved a snack break first.

"One, two, three, and a boom, boom, BOOM!" counted {{FRIEND_NAME}}, and your band burst into the loud, joyful version. The drums rumbled, {{SECOND_NAME}} sang out brave and bright, and {{PET_NAME}} squawked every silly chorus perfectly. The neighbors clapped along, and someone's grandpa did a little wiggle dance in his lawn chair. When the last note boomed, the whole yard cheered, "More! More!" {{SECOND_NAME}} looked at you, glowing, and said, "I was not scared at all. Okay, I was, but then I was not." You all took a bow together, one loud, joyful, wonderful band.

You began soft, like the very first star coming out. {{SECOND_NAME}}'s voice floated over {{FRIEND_NAME}}'s gentle, careful beat, and {{PET_NAME}} cooed along so tenderly that even the babies in the crowd went quiet to listen. "I am being gentle," {{FRIEND_NAME}} whispered proudly, "and I love it, but do not tell the drums." When the song ended, the neighbors did not shout, they just sighed a warm, happy sigh and clapped soft and long. {{SECOND_NAME}} squeezed your hand and said, "Let's do this again next week." And your whole backyard band agreed, because the sweetest sound of all was the four of you together.
